taxonomyNote: ADW treats elk/wapiti and red deer as one species, Cervus elaphus, with regional variation; North Ground's separate red-deer record may need a scope note.
fieldMarks: Dark brown in winter, tan in summer, with buff rump patch
Males carry large antlers and a dark neck-to-chest mane; 178-497 kg
behavior: Herds up to 400; males hold harems in the fall rut (late Sept-early Oct) and bugle
Browses early morning and evening; inactive by day
habitat: Open woodland avoiding dense forest: conifer swamps, clearcuts, aspen-hardwood; sea level to 3,000 m.
range: Formerly across the Northern Hemisphere; in North America now largely western. Introduced to Ireland, Argentina, Chile, Australia and New Zealand.

lookalikes.name: White-tailed deer
lookalikes.howToTell: Occupies similar habitat but is much smaller (source only notes association).
